business_quality_reasoning: 161 Google reviews at 5.0 indicates a busy, established electrician operation with real demand. No Companies House match was found, so the entity is unverified, but the review volume and multi-area site structure show a going concern.
price_point_reasoning: Emergency and domestic electrical work (rewires, consumer units, fault-finding) typically bills £150-£300 per job; no prices shown.
modernity_gap: A functional Elementor landing page rather than a full site — serviceable layout but thin, with a broken map embed and no proof elements on the page.
site_weaknesses: The Google Maps embed fails with 'Coordinates of this location not found' — a broken element left visible mid-page
This is a thin SEO service-area page: one paragraph, a bullet list and a phone number, with nothing that builds trust
161 five-star Google reviews are not shown on the page — a 'Reviews' nav link makes visitors leave the funnel to find them
No pricing guidance, response-time promise or named engineer — the page offers urgency but no reassurance
Single CTA is a phone call; no form, quote request or WhatsApp option beyond a floating icon
site_analysis: The captured page is a thin location landing page: hero image, one bullet list of services, a phone CTA and a visibly broken map. It is competent enough on mobile and the navigation hints at a fuller site, but nothing on this page converts — no reviews, accreditations or pricing. For a business with 161 five-star reviews, the page wastes its strongest sales asset.
review_summary: The page we found is a bare-bones area page: a photo, a list of services and a phone number, plus a map box that shows an error message instead of your location. Your 161 five-star reviews do not appear anywhere on it. Putting your reviews and credentials directly on the page would give people a reason to call you instead of the next electrician on Google.
outreach_angle: Your Dulwich page shows a broken map error and none of your 161 five-star reviews — the page undersells you badly.
